module_title: Morphology of Plants & Animal Tissues (Detailed Foundational)
introduction: This foundational level explores the external structures (morphology) of flowering plants and the fundamental building blocks of animals (tissues). Mastery of these basic structural modifications and tissue categorizations is essential for scoring in direct, fact-based NEET questions.

core_concepts.title: Morphology of Root, Stem, and Leaf
core_concepts.description:
1. Root: Develops from the radicle. Regions: Root cap, Meristematic activity, Elongation, and Maturation (bears root hairs). Modifications: Storage (Carrot, Sweet potato), Prop roots (Banyan), Stilt roots (Maize/Sugarcane), Pneumatophores (Rhizophora for respiration).
2. Stem: Develops from the plumule. Bears nodes and internodes. Modifications: Underground storage (Potato, Ginger, Turmeric), Tendrils (Grapevines, Gourds), Thorns (Citrus, Bougainvillea), Phylloclade (Opuntia, Euphorbia).
3. Leaf: Lateral, flattened structure born on a node. Consists of Leaf base, Petiole, and Lamina. Venation: Reticulate (Dicots) vs. Parallel (Monocots). Phyllotaxy (arrangement): Alternate (China rose, Mustard), Opposite (Calotropis, Guava), Whorled (Alstonia, Nerium).

core_concepts.title: The Flower: Basic Whorls
core_concepts.description:
A modified shoot serving as the reproductive unit.
1. Calyx (Sepals): Outermost whorl, protects the bud. (Polysepalous vs. Gamosepalous).
2. Corolla (Petals): Brightly colored to attract pollinators. (Polypetalous vs. Gamopetalous).
3. Androecium (Stamens): Male reproductive organ. Consists of a filament and an anther.
4. Gynoecium (Carpels/Pistils): Female reproductive organ. Consists of Stigma, Style, and Ovary.

core_concepts.title: Animal Tissues: Epithelial & Connective
core_concepts.description:
1. Epithelial Tissue: Covers body surfaces and lines cavities. Squamous (diffusion boundaries - alveoli, blood vessels), Cuboidal (secretion/absorption - nephrons, ducts), Columnar (stomach, intestines), Ciliated (moves particles in a specific direction - bronchioles, fallopian tubes).
2. Connective Tissue: Most abundant. Links and supports other tissues. Loose (Areolar, Adipose), Dense Regular (Tendons, Ligaments), Dense Irregular (Skin), and Specialized (Cartilage, Bone, Blood).

core_concepts.title: Animal Tissues: Muscular & Neural
core_concepts.description:
1. Muscular Tissue: Skeletal (striated, voluntary, multinucleated), Smooth (non-striated, involuntary, fusiform/spindle-shaped, found in organs), Cardiac (striated, involuntary, branched, intercalated discs).
2. Neural Tissue: Neurons are the excitable cells. Neuroglial cells make up more than half the volume of neural tissue and protect/support neurons.

important_entities.name: Tendons vs. Ligaments
important_entities.key_fact: Tendons connect Muscle to Bone; Ligaments connect Bone to Bone.
important_entities.significance: Both are examples of Dense Regular Connective Tissue. In dense regular tissues, the collagen fibers are arranged in parallel bundles between many parallel bundles of fibers, providing immense tensile strength in one direction.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
A massive source of confusion in NEET. You MUST specify the origin. 
Stem Tendrils develop from axillary buds (e.g., Gourds like cucumber, pumpkins, watermelon, and Grapevines). 
Leaf Tendrils develop from the modification of leaves or leaflets (e.g., Peas/Pisum sativum).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Alstonia Whorls; Alternate is China's Mustard Sun; Opposite is Guava Calotropis
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
- Whorled: Alstonia, Nerium.
- Alternate: China rose, Mustard, Sunflower.
- Opposite: Guava, Calotropis.

exam_strategy_tips: In animal tissues, always link the structure to its function. For example, 'diffusion' requires the thinnest possible layer, so Squamous epithelium is the answer. 'Moving mucus or an ovum' requires sweeping action, so Ciliated epithelium is the answer.
